title: Thinking about firing someone post-close? Read this first.

 Let’s make sure your post-close transitions don’t go full Succession

 Thinking about firing someone post-close? Read this first.
Hi Sara,
Let’s talk about one of the most uncomfortable (and often mishandled) parts of post-deal integration:
Letting someone go.
If that’s something you’re considering after a deal closes, here’s my advice:
You don’t need to be an HR genius.
But you do need to avoid rookie mistakes that burn bridges, rattle morale, or land you in hot water.
I’ve sat in on more of these conversations than I can count—some with tissues, some with lawyers, and one that felt like a deleted scene from Succession.
Here’s what experience has taught me:
Clarity is kindness. You can be empathetic and still get to the point. No need to monologue.

Skip the warm-up. Please don’t chat about someone’s weekend before delivering bad news. It doesn’t soften the blow—it just makes it weirder.

Less is more. You don’t need to justify the decision five different ways. Say what needs to be said, then stop talking.

If you’re planning post-close transitions, whether it’s one role or a full team reorg, the how matters just as much as the what.
I recently recorded a video on how to keep top talent post close (not legal advice—just the real-world stuff no one tells you).
Got your own hard-learned lesson or save-the-day script? Hit reply—I’m always collecting wisdom from the trenches.

To smarter structuring,
Sara Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Founder, Deal Academy
